results.eligibility_evidence: LLM screening: “We aimed to validate large language models (LLMs) used to automate abstract screening.” Human reference: “LLMs exhibited superior performance to human researchers in terms of sensitivity (LLMmax = 1.000, humanmax = 0.775)”. Accuracy: “consistent sensitivity (range 0.756-1.000) but diminished precision (range 0.004-0.096)”. Original study: “trialed across 23 Cochrane Library systematic reviews to evaluate their accuracy in zero-shot binary classification for abstract screening”.
results.screening_note: Judged on title/abstract only. Sensitivity and precision are reported; specificity is not named in the abstract, but sensitivity alone satisfies the accuracy criterion.

results.eligibility_evidence: LLM screening: “We evaluated GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Llama 3.1:8B on abstract screening and risk of bias assessment using 12 Cochrane drug intervention reviews.” Human reference: “Validation Based on Cochrane Review Data” (title). Accuracy: “GPT-4o achieved the best screening performance (recall 0.894, precision 0.492)”. Original study: “We propose a one-shot inclusivity adjustment method”.
results.screening_note: Judged on title/abstract only. The reference standard is taken to be the Cochrane reviews' (human) inclusion decisions; the abstract does not state this explicitly, so confirm at full text.

failed_criteria.evidence_quote: Screening and extraction process took place in Covidence with the help of LLM add-on based on the OpenAI GPT-4o model.

failed_criteria.evidence_quote: Our LLM-assisted systematic review revealed a significant number of research projects related to review automation using LLMs.

failed_criteria.evidence_quote: the former was better in data extraction with a mean precision of 83.0% (SD = 10.4) and a recall of 86.0%

results.eligibility_evidence: LLM screening: “LLM-assisted screening was performed using ChatGPT-4o (OpenAI) and Claude-3.5 (Anthropic) sonnet”. Human reference: “Manual screening by 2 investigators served as the reference standard.” Accuracy: “Title and abstract screening achieved a pooled sensitivity of 0.73 (95% CI 0.57-0.85) and specificity of 0.99”. Original study: “We conducted a diagnostic study comparing the accuracy of LLM-assisted screening versus manual literature screening across 6 thoracic surgery meta-analyses.”
results.screening_note: Judged on title/abstract only. Reports title/abstract and full-text screening accuracy separately, plus comparisons with ASReview and Abstrackr.

results.eligibility_evidence: LLM screening: “recommending inclusion/exclusion decisions during abstract screening”. Human reference: “indicating substantial agreement between human reviewers and LLM-based results”. Accuracy: “it achieved an average sensitivity of 90%, F1 score of 82, accuracy of 89%, and Cohen's κ of 0.71”. Original study: “We developed and validated a large language model (LLM)-assisted system for conducting systematic literature reviews”.
results.screening_note: Judged on title/abstract only. Human-in-the-loop system for HTA reviews; specificity is not named in the abstract, but sensitivity is reported.
